description.value:
Price 1,500 gp; Usage single use

An Androffan auto-injector that plays a short burst of recorded applause as it fires. It heals 4d8+10 hit points and grants @UUID[Compendium.pf1.spells.Item.rgd5v3llwoptwcdb]{good hope} for 1 minute. Injecting takes a standard action.

Trinket (d8: 1). Celmak hands these out when the ratings reach 5.

Price 1,200 gp; Usage single use

The user is @UUID[Compendium.pf1.spells.Item.s9amdo5398alb5p0]{hasted} for 5 rounds, then fatigued for 1 minute.

Trinket (d8: 2).

Price 300 gp; Usage single use

Immunity to inhaled effects, including Mood Gas, for 1 hour.

Trinket (d8: 3).

Price 600 gp; Usage single use

Thrown 30 ft.; bright light in a 60-ft radius for 1 minute, and outlines invisible creatures as @UUID[Compendium.pf1.spells.Item.bl71og1gklwncmt7]{faerie fire}.

Trinket (d8: 4). Light is the enemy of shadows, and the friend of holograms.

effect: Bright light 60 ft.; outlines invisible creatures

description.value:
Price 2,000 gp; Capacity 3; Usage 1 charge per use

A disc that projects 1d4 duplicates of the user, as @UUID[Compendium.pf1.spells.Item.4jsss37x0pplib8f]{mirror image}.

Trinket (d8: 5).

Price 900 gp; Usage single use

20-ft burst; robots take 6d6 electricity damage (Reflex DC 18 half) and their force fields lose fast healing for 1 round.

Trinket (d8: 6). Celmak considers this one a little unsporting.

effect: Robots only; force fields lose fast healing 1 round

description.value:
Price 500 gp; Usage single use

A slip of film showing Celmak's next twist. Once, as an immediate action, gain a +4 insight bonus on one saving throw inside the Garden.

Trinket (d8: 7).

Price up to 5,000 gp

A magic item from a dead adventurer, chosen to help just enough. Replace this card with an item worth up to 5,000 gp, ideally one whose owner is named in the Ledger of the Fallen.

Trinket (d8: 8).

Price 28,000 gp; Slot neck; Weight —; Capacity 10; Usage 2 charges per pulse

A mesh of silver filaments that settles into the skin of the throat. The wearer gains a +5 competence bonus on Knowledge (engineering) checks and a +2 bonus on caster level checks against constructs. When the wearer casts a spell or uses a nanite-based ability, they can spend a swift action to emit an override pulse: every robot within 30 feet must succeed at a DC 20 Will save or be staggered for 1 round. A wearer with the nanite bloodline treats the lattice's save DC as 22.

Construction Requirements Craft Technological Item, military lab; Cost 14,000 gp; Craft DC 28.

Found in: Episode 1 (the Prize Sentinel's chest case).

save.description: Will negates (robots; DC 22 for nanite bloodline)

description.value:
Price 26,000 gp; Slot head; Weight 1 lb.; Capacity 10; Usage 1 charge per scan

Celmak's own mind-scanning optics, salvaged from her body. The party gets it only if Celmak is destroyed, surrenders, or hands it over as part of a deal. The wearer gains a +5 competence bonus on Sense Motive checks. As a standard action, the wearer can scan one creature within 60 feet, as @UUID[Compendium.pf1.spells.Item.xllxylvvqr82o2d5]{detect thoughts} with all three rounds of information gained at once (Will DC 20 negates).

Construction Requirements Craft Technological Item, military lab; Cost 13,000 gp; Craft DC 28.

Found in: Celmak (the Cutting Room).

Aura moderate conjuration; Cl 13th; Slot none; Price 25,000 gp; Weight —

A living acorn grown from the awakened Lock Tree. While carried, it grants a +2 insight bonus on saves against illusions: its bearer can feel what is real. Planted in the Hollow Garden's dome after the Core is shut down, it turns the synthetic garden into a living fey glade over a month. Planted anywhere else, it grows overnight into a 200-foot-wide grove where the bearer and their allies can always rest undisturbed, as @UUID[Compendium.pf1.spells.Item.9v2s3xjlakjm1eq1]{private sanctum}. Once planted, it is used up.

Construction Requirements none; it grows only from the Lock Tree.

Found in: Episode 4, if the Tree was awakened rather than disabled or smashed.

Price 16,000 gp; Slot wrist; Weight 1 lb.; Capacity 10; Usage 3 charges per use

As a move action, the wearer projects either a hard-light shield, granting a +4 shield bonus to AC (a force effect), or a hard-light blade that functions as a +2 short sword dealing force damage. Either lasts 1 minute. Darkness suppresses the effect while the wearer stands in it.

Construction Requirements Craft Technological Arms and Armor, military lab; Cost 8,000 gp; Craft DC 26.

Found in: Episode 1.

Price 12,000 gp; Slot none; Weight 8 lb.; Capacity 10; Usage 5 charges per use

A folding maintenance cradle from the Divinity's android workshops, “complimentary with purchase.” An android or other construct that rests in it for 10 minutes regains 10d6 hit points and is cured of one of the following conditions: fatigued, sickened, staggered or confused. It also lets its user find and purge factory override phrases, like the one Celmak holds over Meyanda, without a check.

Construction Requirements Craft Technological Item, military lab; Cost 6,000 gp; Craft DC 26.

Found in: Mint Condition (Meyanda's episode).

effect: Androids/constructs only; also cures fatigued, sickened, staggered or confused

description.value:
Price 9,000 gp; Slot none; Weight —; Capacity 3; Usage 1 charge per use

A cartridge from the holographic bridge's captain's chair that should not exist yet. As an immediate action after rolling a d20, but before the result is announced, the holder can reroll and take the better result. A kasatha raised by a time traveller may use it without the charge being spent once per day: it simply remembers how.

Construction Requirements none; its origin is unknown.

Found in: Episode 3.

effect: Reroll a d20, take the better result

description.value:
Price 4,000 gp; Type exotic light melee weapon; Damage 1d6 (Small), 1d8 (Medium); Critical 18–20/×2; Damage Type slashing; Weight 1 lb.

A folding fan whose ribs carry monofilament edges. It can be used with Weapon Finesse and ignores the first 10 points of an object's hardness. A creature wielding one in each hand counts as wielding a light weapon in its off hand.

Found in: Episode 2. Each Courtier Mannequin carries a pair.

Price 4,000 gp; Slot none; Weight —

A palm-sized Androffan memory crystal that plays back, in light and sound, the evening the kasatha ambassadors spent on the entertainment deck. Once per day, a kasatha who spends a minute watching it gains a +2 morale bonus on attack rolls and Will saves for 1 hour.

Found in: Episode 2 (Lot 5) or The Ambassadors.

effect: Kasatha: +2 morale on attacks and Will saves

description.value:
Price 3,000 gp; Slot none; Weight —

A data spike holding the Lock Tree's engineering drawings, hand-drawn by a dead Technic League engineer. Celmak did not write it, so it is immune to the honeypots. Plugged into any reader, it grants a +5 bonus on checks to find, disable or understand the Dimensional Anchor Array. Afterward, it grants a +2 bonus on checks against any Androffan dimensional anchor, which may matter at Silver Mount.

Found in: Episode 2 (Lot 4). Vlathherex bids on this and nothing else.

Price 2,000 gp; Slot none; Weight 1 lb.

A datapad listing every adventurer who died in the Garden, with their gear, their home towns and their heirs. Its holder gains a +4 bonus on Diplomacy checks with anyone named in it or related to someone who is. Once, it identifies the original owner of one item in the hoard of the fallen.

Found in: Episode 2 (Lot 1).

Price priceless; Slot none; Weight —

A data spike holding the entertainment deck's records, partial crew logs and Celmak's footage of every contestant. Its owner gains a +4 bonus on Knowledge checks about the Divinity, Silver Mount and Androffans. It also holds one secret of your choice, such as a maintenance route into Silver Mount, crew lists, or logs from before Unity went mad.

Found in: The 113th Take (Casandalee's episode).

Auction scrip for The Last Market (Episode 2). Each contestant receives 2 on entry (14 for the party).

Raising more: sell a true secret (2 each), sell blood (1 per 10 hp, unhealable until the episode ends), lend a companion to the Box (3 each), or sell an item (1 per 5,000 gp of value).

Worthless outside the Garden. Celmak honours every sale.

“A fetchling's shadow lantern: your door home!” (Open 3, rival max 8)

A fake: a hologram wrapped around an empty lantern. Using it reveals the dimensional lock: the Shadow Plane feels sealed, like a door painted onto a wall. Celmak laughs: “Nobody leaves early. Rule three.”

“A Producer's Share: a cut of the house, for one lucky contestant.” (Open 1, rival max 1)

A trap. Whoever signs must make a DC 25 Will save or be bound as @UUID[Compendium.pf1.spells.Item.ofw6gnp6r7t2wcba]{lesser geas} not to leave the Garden before the finale. Sense Motive DC 25 reveals the catch.

C4rUqswjLzfLFI7H.name: Lot 6: A Grab Bag from the Vaults

description.value:
“A grab bag from the vaults.” (Open 3, rival max 7)

2 applause injectors and a ring of freedom of movement.

QndOLaJGvrUkJ66X.name: Lot 7: Last Words of the Bright Lanterns

description.value:
“Last words of the Bright Lanterns. Very sad. Very long.” (Open 2, rival max 4)

The final recording of the last adventuring party. It runs three hours. Its last ten minutes show four exhausted adventurers crawling through a maintenance duct behind the Showroom's seventh plinth, reaching a hatch into the Core Vault before a drone finds them.

  • The crawlway route into the Core Vault, which lets the party skip the vault door in the finale.
  • A cache in the duct: 3 applause injectors and a scroll of @UUID[Compendium.pf1.spells.Item.e5kw4dwf9qwty6tl]{greater dispel magic}.
  • The Lanterns' leader whispering, “She's not in the Booth. The Booth is a doll. She's down.”

Celmak never watched past hour one. When she realises what she sold, she drops the ratings by 1.

“A Genuine Celmak Original! Your portrait, by the artist herself.” (Open 1, rival max 3)

A flattering hologram portrait of the winner. It is also a camera drone that follows the winner everywhere: Celmak gains a +2 bonus on Muse scans against them. Destroying it costs 1 rating; Celmak sulks for an hour.

“Thirty Seconds of Silence. Well. One episode of it.” (Open 3, rival max 9)

A voucher. For one episode of the winner's choice, Celmak gives no commentary and opens no Mood Gas vents. She bids high on this herself; she hates silence.

“Paperwork! The cast's original contract.” (Open 2, rival max 5)

The deal Vlathherex's demons signed with Celmak. The fine print promises them roles “for the full run of the show,” which has no end date. The winner gains a +4 bonus on Diplomacy and Intimidate checks with the cast.

“The Mystery Box. Nobody knows. Not even me.” (Open 1, rival max 2)

Roll 1d6 on the Mystery Box roll table.

“Exhibit G. Feeds itself. Mostly harmless.” (Open 2, rival max 6)

A stasis cube holding Ivo Marrant (NE male human wizard 9), a Technic League initiate who came looking for the Garden two years ago. Released, he is starving, terrified and still arrogant. He knows the League has a file on the Garden and has lost three agents here; he will trade everything he knows about the League's presence in Starfall for his life, and will betray the party the moment it suits him.

“A Front-Row Seat for the next episode. The best view in the house.” (Open 4, rival max 8)

The winner sits out the next episode in the Booth's guest box, completely safe. The Booth is lit, full of monitors, and empty except for a single mannequin slumped in the director's chair with its eyes dark. Whenever Celmak speaks, its eyes glow and its head turns. A DC 20 Perception check shows a thick data cable running from its spine into the floor.

“A Second Act. Everyone deserves one.” (Open 3, rival max 7)
